candidates.name: Integral character classes z_i(t)
paper_items: supporting: I39 orbit sheaf / eigensheaves (06:25-35), I40 character coproducts, I41 real orthogonality, I43 sum = 2[A,alpha], I44 covariance, I45 homotopy invariance, I28 contractible-quotient integral iso (04:487-529)
candidates.statement: For a compact test t: Y -> X and a finite partition Lambda = D_0 u ... u D_{m-1} of the p-power roots of unity, z_i(t) in E_d(X) = W_d(T(X)) is the unique integral class with l_U(z_i) = [A_t, alpha_t] + [A_t, alpha_t(2e_i - 1)] in W_d(T(X)/T(U)), where e_i are the self-adjoint character projectors on the punctured target and l_U is the integral localization iso for a contractible U around b_t (d odd).

neighbours.ref: Atiyah-Singer, The index of elliptic operators III, Ann. Math. 87 (1968), G-signature theorem; Gilmer, A topological proof of the G-signature theorem for G finite, Pacific J. Math. 97 (1981)
neighbours.relation: For a finite group G acting on an oriented manifold, the signature form on H^mid(M;C) splits into isotypic parts with integral signatures; Sign(G,M) lies in the representation ring R(G). For an involution sigma, [b] + [b(sigma.,.)] = 2[b restricted to the +1 eigenspace]: exactly the [A,alpha] + [A, alpha(2e-1)] identity, with 2e-1 the involution. For free actions, sign(g,M) = 0 for g != 1, so all isotypic multiplicities are equal (dim rho * sigma/|G|).
neighbours.verdict: close variant (finite-group, closed-manifold ancestor of the profinite, germ-localized Witt version)

neighbours.ref: Hirzebruch-Zagier, The Atiyah-Singer theorem and elementary number theory (1974); cited by the F1 agent (f1_character_classes.json)
neighbours.relation: Involution signatures: sign(V+-) = (sign b +- sign(T,M))/2, i.e. the reflection-twist identity [V,b] + [V,b(2e-1)] = 2[eV] in classical form.
neighbours.verdict: equivalent for the algebraic kernel of the device (not for the localized profinite construction)

final.justification: A close variant exists: isotypic signature classes for finite group actions (Atiyah-Singer, Gilmer, CSW), including the identity [b] + [b*sigma] = 2[b|V+] for an involution. 304's contribution is to make this work for a profinite group with infinite-dimensional character parts and a non-manifold orbit space. It does so by germ-localizing projectors on the punctured target, lifting integrally through a contractible quotient with d odd, and taking 2x the summand to avoid splitting idempotents. These are real but technical adaptations of a known invariant, which is N2. The family analyst's provisional N3 (F1/F5) is downgraded because the finite-group equal-parts template is classical and the analyst did not name it. Upgrade to N3 (F1) only if an expert judges the profinite localized lift to need an idea absent from the finite-group theory, and Test 4's template arm stays below threshold.

family_D.not_transfer: The method fields (Verdier duality, triangular Witt groups, Hardt triviality, Serre's odd spheres) are transfers (N0). The candidates are adaptations and couplings, so the transfer exclusion caps nothing beyond N2 here.
family_D.correctness_caveat: All grades are conditional on correctness. This is an unreviewed claimed proof of a famous open conjecture, with no Lean and no trace. The family analyst found no gap but flags the Witt theory of the non-constructible categories T (Balmer-Walter hypotheses on quotients, dense doubling, germ theorem) as the crux. The AI-assisted Coppola audit independently grades dense doubling, the Balmer-Walter bridge, character coproducts and the equal-parts isometry as WEAK (no FAIL). There is no expert reaction yet as of 2026-10-09.
family_D.compression_note: No Lean, so there is no step-3b compression measurement. Qualitatively the character classes are a single-use bottleneck: they compress a whole cohomological-dimension programme (Yang/BRW) into a 4-line counting argument, but the cost is moved into about 1.5k lines of Witt/sheaf foundations (C6-C8).
